title: Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous opens at The Met Fifth Avenue
summary: Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous at The Metropolitan Museum of Art is a major exhibition that charts the full arc of the careers of Lee Krasner (1908–1984) and Jackson Pollock (1912–1956) in parallel, examining the distinct yet connected practices of these artistic peers and life partners. On view October 4, 2026, through January 31, 2027, it marks the first major New York presentation devoted to either artist in more than 20 years, introducing their work to a new generation while reassessing their enduring impacts on modern and contemporary art. Krasner and Pollock were emerging artists in New York when they met on the occasion of being included in a 1942 exhibition organized by the artist John Graham. They married in 1945 and moved to Springs, Long Island, where they remained entwined personally, artistically, and professionally until Pollock’s death in 1956. title: Georgia Museum of Art hires Michael Neumeister in curatorial leadership position
summary: Following a national search, the Georgia Museum of Art at the University of Georgia has hired Michael Neumeister as its deputy director of curatorial and academic affairs and curator of American art, effective September 15. He will be responsible for setting the museum’s curatorial vision across its wide-ranging collections and exhibition program. Tricia Miller, interim director of the museum, said, “We are so pleased to welcome Michael Neumeister to the curatorial team at the Georgia Museum of Art. He brings a wealth of leadership and curatorial experience to the position, and we look forward to seeing his vision for the Georgia Museum unfold.” Neumeister was most recently senior curator at the Columbia Museum of Art (CMA), in Columbia, South Carolina, where he led exhibition programming and directed collections growth and care. title: ACES Gallery announces highlights included in Fall Estates Auction
summary: More than 450 lots of distinguished provenance, carefully curated from nearly 50 prominent local estates, will come up for bid in ACES Gallery ’s Fall Estates Auction on Sunday, October 18th. Categories will include contemporary and fine art; Western art; decorative arts; Asian art; silver; watches and timepieces; jewelry; collectibles; and books. The auction will begin promptly at 12 noon Eastern Time. Bidding will be available online, with telephone and absentee bidding also available. There will be no live in-person bidding, however. Internet bidding will be facilitated by LiveAuctioneers.com, Invaluable.com and Drouot.com. title: Vermeer's 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' returns to the Mauritshuis after Japan visit
summary: Johannes Vermeer’s Girl with a Pearl Earring is returning home to the Mauritshuis after a five-week stay in Japan, where the celebrated painting drew some 280,000 visitors during a special exhibition at the Nakanoshima Museum of Art in Osaka. The painting will go back on view at the Mauritshuis on Monday, October 5, bringing to a close one of the rare occasions on which the museum has allowed its most famous work to travel abroad. To mark its return, the Mauritshuis will hold a brief press event attended by Martine Gosselink, the museum’s General Director, Jan van Zanen, Mayor of The Hague, and Rokuichiro Michii, Japan’s ambassador to the Netherlands. During the event, Girl with a Pearl Earring will be rehung in Gallery 15, where visitors will once again be able to encounter Vermeer’s enigmatic figure in its familiar setting. title: Major monograph of Robert Indiana coming from Phaidon this fall
summary: Robert Indiana is one of the most significant artists of the twentieth century. Emerging in the 1960s, his bold work explored themes of American identity, personal narrative, and the power of color, form, and language. Known for his contributions to Pop art, assemblage, sculpture, and hard-edge painting, Indiana was deeply attuned to the historical, linguistic, and psychological structures that have shaped America’s identity. His transformation of words and numbers he personally identified with into universally legible symbols resonates across generations of artists and audiences who followed him. Robert Indiana: An American Icon is a comprehensive survey of his life and career. Created in close collaboration with The Robert Indiana Legacy Initiative, this landmark volume invites readers to rediscover Indiana through more than 450 career-spanning images of his paintings, sculpture, and works

title: Perrotin mounts career-spanning solo exhibition for Young-Il Ahn
summary: Perrotin announced Young-Il Ahn: Self Reflections, the first solo presentation of works by Korean-American artist Young-Il Ahn (1934–2020) at Perrotin New York, and the second exhibition since the gallery announced representation of the estate in 2025. Featuring ten paintings from his celebrated Water series, along with a selection of abstractions spanning his fifty-year career of painting in California, Young-Il Ahn: Self Reflections highlights the deeply personal and autobiographical nature of the artist’s practice. Displayed alongside the Water paintings are works from additional series including Harbor, Musicians, Horse Race, Memorial to September 11, 2001, as well as the eponymous Self Reflection series to which the exhibition title nods. title: Neuberger Museum of Art Director Tracy Fitzpatrick announces plans for June 2027 retirement
summary: The Neuberger Museum of Art at SUNY Purchase announced today that Tracy [Schpero] Fitzpatrick, the Museum’s eighth director, will retire from the State University of New York (SUNY) system effective June 30, 2027, after over a decade of leadership as director of the Neuberger, two decades of service to the Neuberger, and thirty-six years in the field. Under her leadership, the Neuberger produced exhibitions, publications, and educational initiatives that connected students, faculty, artists, and audiences of all ages while strengthening the relationship between academic learning and direct engagement with works in the Museum’s permanent collection and by visiting artists. title: Kiasma announces its exhibition programme 2027
summary: In 2027, Kiasma will present the most extensive exhibition to date in the Nordic countries by acclaimed contemporary British artist Antony Gormley. Alongside Gormley’s exhibition, two solo exhibitions will introduce the work of leading international artists: Monster Chetwynd will transform the museum’s top floor into an imaginative world where visitors are invited to become part of the artwork, while Ann Lislegaard’s exhibition will bring together a wide selection of works spanning different stages of her career. In the autumn, Kiasma will present a group exhibition featuring the four nominees for Ars Fennica, Finland’s most prestigious contemporary art prize. The museum’s new collection exhibition will offer a comprehensive overview of Kalervo Palsa’s oeuvre, bringing his work into dialogue with contemporary artists whose themes and artistic approaches echo those found in Palsa’s art. title: Brueghel masterpiece leads strong results at Koller September auctions
summary: Strong bidding and numerous results above the pre-sale estimates characterised Koller’s September auctions. The Dr Peter Ducret Collection of 18th-century faïence was particularly successful, with 90% of the lots finding buyers and total hammer prices reaching 185% of the low estimates. Pieter Brueghel the Younger’s ‘The Swan Inn’ was another highlight, selling for CHF 1.34 million and becoming the tenth lot to surpass the million-franc mark at Koller this year. One of the highlights of the autumn auction series was the Collection of Dr Peter Ducret. The son of the esteemed porcelain expert Siegfried Ducret, Dr Ducret devoted his life to the study and collection of 18th-century faïence. A remarkable group of trompe-l’oeil serving pieces, many produced by the Hannong dynasty in Strasbourg, attracted particularly spirited bidding. title: Kimbell announces 2027 exhibitions
summary: The Kimbell Art Museum today announced two special exhibitions for 2027: Treasures of the Pharaohs in the spring, followed by Thomas Gainsborough opening in the fall. The Kimbell will be one of only two museums in North America to display 130 carefully selected artifacts from the Egyptian Museum in Cairo and the Luxor Museum, offering rare insights into the daily life, social structures, religious practices, and legacies of the Egyptian pharaohs. title: Louvre-Lens explores the irresistible—and unsettling—power of cuteness in new exhibition
summary: Why do round faces, soft toys, pink rooms and wide-eyed animals make us feel instantly protective, amused or comforted? A new exhibition at the Louvre-Lens takes that deceptively simple question seriously. So Cute! The Art of Happiness, now on view through January 18, 2027, brings together more than 300 works and objects to trace the history, psychology and visual language of cuteness from antiquity to the present day. Rather than treating “cute” as a passing internet phenomenon, the exhibition looks at it as a powerful emotional code that artists, designers, advertisers and political movements have used for centuries. title: Marlow Moss returns to the spotlight in London with rare works from private collections
summary: More than half a century after her last commercial solo presentation in her hometown, British abstract artist Marlow Moss is returning to the London spotlight with Marlow Moss: Space, Movement & Light, an exhibition at Ward Moretti that brings together rarely seen works from private collections. The exhibition seeks to reposition Moss within the history of European modernism, where her contribution to Constructivism and Neoplasticism has often been overshadowed by that of her friend and contemporary Piet Mondrian. Ward Moretti describes the show as the first commercial solo presentation of Moss in London in more than 50 years and an opportunity to reconsider an artist whose rigorous geometric language developed alongside, rather than simply in imitation of, her better-known peers. Born Marjorie Jewel Moss in London in 1889, the artist moved through several phases of experimentation before settling in Paris in 1927, then the center of the international avant-garde.

title: The Vancouver Art Gallery confirms Eva Respini and Sirish Rao as Co-CEOs
summary: The Vancouver Art Gallery Association Board of Trustees today announced the permanent appointment of Eva Respini and Sirish Rao as Co-CEOs, confirming a dual leadership model designed to advance the Gallery’s artistic ambition, operational resilience and global reach. The decision reflects the Board's confidence in Respini and Rao's leadership over the past year, during which they strengthened the Gallery's financial position, deepened its commitment to art, artists and community, and established a renewed vision for the institution's future. This announcement follows a rigorous evaluation process undertaken by the Governance and People Committee of the Board. title: BnF traces 80 years of Japanese photography in major Paris exhibition
summary: Eight decades of Japanese photography, from the social realism of the postwar years to the quiet strangeness of contemporary everyday life, come into focus at the Bibliothèque nationale de France in a major exhibition opening September 30. Japanese Photographs from the Bibliothèque nationale de France, 1945-2025: Scenes, Signs, Sensations brings together some 300 works by around 100 photographers at the BnF's François-Mitterrand site, offering a broad view of a collection that the institution has been building for more than half a century. The exhibition draws on holdings that now encompass nearly 4,000 photographic prints by about 200 artists and reporters, along with roughly 100 magazines and landmark books. title: Spectacular new installation of 2,000 books unveiled inside Es Devlin's first European retrospective
summary: A vast rotating library has been unveiled today at the Design Museum in London, as the newly-announced finale of a major exhibition exploring the work of British artist and designer Es Devlin. An Infinite Library is a remarkable new kinetic sculpture featuring over 2,000 books that have informed Devlin’s worldview. Arranged by colour, many are well thumbed copies drawn directly from Devlin’s studio bookshelves, including Chaos by James Gleick, The Spell of the Sensuous by David Abram, Beloved by Toni Morrison and Oryx and Crake by Margaret Atwood. The eight-metre-wide triangular bookshelf rotates on a circular mirror, invoking Umberto Eco’s description of a library as a compass of the mind. title: Billy Joel's personal motorcycle collection set for unreserved debut at Rétromobile New York
summary: Gooding Christie's, the official auction house of Rétromobile New York, has announced the world-famous Billy Joel Motorcycle Collection as its first major consignment for its upcoming inaugural sale at the Javits Center in New York City. The Rétromobile New York Auctions, taking place on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21, will feature over 70 lots from the legendary recording artist's collection, presented entirely without reserve. Select offerings from the Billy Joel Motorcycle Collection will be displayed at Christie's Rockefeller Center from October 8-12. Interested media and clientele are encouraged to reach out to the auction house to scheduling viewing appointments in advance. title: Mexico and France continue dialogue over possible return of the Codex Borbonicus
summary: Mexico and France will continue discussions over the possible repatriation of the Codex Borbonicus, one of the most important surviving pictorial manuscripts associated with Mexica ritual and calendrical traditions, as communities in Hidalgo renew calls for its return ahead of the New Fire ceremony expected in 2027. The issue emerged during the closing of the Mexico-France International Symposium on Mesoamerican Codices, an event that brought together scholars, cultural officials and Indigenous communities to examine the history, preservation and contemporary meaning of manuscripts that have survived from the centuries surrounding the Spanish conquest. title: Art Gallery of NSW and National Gallery of Australia announce collaboration to share significant artworks
summary: The Art Gallery of New South Wales and the National Gallery of Australia have announced a landmark collaboration that will see significant works by internationally renowned artists Edvard Munch and Njideka Akunyili Crosby shared between the two institutions. Under the agreement, Man with horse 1918 by Norwegian master Edvard Munch will be on special loan from the National Gallery to the Art Gallery, with the institutions participating in an alternating cycle of loans, including the Art Gallery’s reciprocal loan of Na Parlour (In the parlor) 2025 by Njideka Akunyili Crosby. One of the most significant international artworks to enter an Australian public collection in recent decades, Man with horse was gifted to the National Gallery in 2024 by philanthropist Geoff Ainsworth AM. summary: Harvard University’s Hutchins Center for African & African American Research announces An Introduction to Van Lévé: Sovereign Visions from the Creole and Maroon Caribbean and Amazonia: Guadeloupe, Martinique, Guyane and Haiti: 2001-Now, on view at the Alain Locke Gallery of African & African American Art, from September 28, 2026, to June 5, 2027. title: Para Site is on the move for 2027 programme
summary: Para Site is on the move! We’re leaving Quarry Bay and working towards a new home in Hong Kong. Our nomadic programme across 2027 gives us room to try things out in different places, nurture collaborations, and rethink how we gather. What we present along the way will help shape the space we build: one that we arrive at with a deeper understanding of what it needs to make possible. That exploration is already underway. "Elsewhere in Me", a series of new live art commissions across Hong Kong throughout this year has included River Lin (My Body is a Para Site) and Tong Wenmin (Towards Solace), and continues with Justin Talplacido Shoulder (Phasmahammer) in November and Yim Sui Fong in December. title: C-LAB to host 2026 Trans-Dimensional Technology and Art Forum in Taiwan
summary: On Friday, October 16, Kong Zong Cultural Base (C-LAB) will be hosting the 2026 Trans-dimensional Technology and Art Forum at the CREATORS' Space Coworking Space, bringing tech art experts to Taiwan for international exchange. Part of the "Skyward 2026" festival series, the Forum highlights C-LAB’s activities in tech art and contemporary creative practice. The C-LAB-organized event aligns with the Industrial Technology Research Institute’s (ITRI) Future Art & Technology Salon in a dual-track initiative. The 2026 Trans-dimensional Technology and Art Forum consists of a morning and an afternoon session. title: Countdown begins as Ipswich Museum announces it is set to reopen in Spring 2027
summary: The transformation of Ipswich Museum is now in its final stages as the Suffolk attraction prepares to reopen its doors and welcome visitors in the early part of next year (2027). The museum closed in October 2022 for the £12million refurbishment to get underway. During that time, the mammoth restorations to the 146-year-old, Grade II listed building have been painstaking, with eight new and upgraded galleries.
